title: Run Lint All (Full Report)
summary: Runs the whole rule catalog against a project's indexed code and reports every surviving finding -- the overall project health check
intro: Read this when you want an overall health check of a project: it runs the whole rule catalog over the indexed code and reports every surviving finding, optionally limited to one project with --project.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Code Quality > Run Lint All (Full Report)...
steps: Open the project in RAD Studio (its index must be current)
Choose drag-lint > Code Quality > Run Lint All (Full Report)...
Read the findings in the report

flags.name: --quiet
flags.summary: suppress per-file progress lines written to stderr

flags.name: --shared-db
flags.summary: another project index, repeatable: evidence for a closure-dependent dl:ok on a dl:shared unit

pitfalls: A second --db is the library slot, not another project: to judge a dl:ok on a dl:shared unit use --shared-db.

`--library-db <lib>` names the library slot too and wins over a second --db and the manifest; a missing file refuses (exit 2), `none` means no library. Without a library, a type whose ancestry lives there stays unknown and the type-aware rules stay silent on it.
lint `<file>` is a strict SUBSET: project-wide rules can only fire in lint-all.
A vendored folder INSIDE the project folder is linted as your own code until `excludeRoots` names it in `<project>\_D-RAG\drag-lint-project.json`.
